title: Advice for Writers from an Aspiring Author
use_cases: Use when designing a new epic world with intricate magic systems and large-scale conflicts.
Implement when setting a story in a realistic, Earth-like environment where magic is a rare anomaly.
Configure when blending contemporary urban settings with hidden supernatural elements for intimate city‑wide narratives.
Use when emphasizing grand, high stakes that involve the fate of entire civilizations.
Implement when focusing on personal dilemmas and localized moral choices within magical or non‑magical contexts.
content:
High fantasy, often referred to as epic fantasy, is characterized by its creation of entirely new, self-contained worlds with their own rules, histories, and mythologies. These worlds are usually separate from our own and feature elaborate settings that include diverse cultures, magical systems, and complex political structures.

Magic is a central element in high fantasy, often woven into the very fabric of the world. The magic system is usually intricate and foundational to the plot and setting. Mythology, including gods, ancient prophecies, and legendary creatures, plays a significant role.

High fantasy stories tend to be grand in scope, often involving epic quests, large-scale conflicts, and world-changing events. The stakes are usually high, with the fate of entire worlds or civilizations at risk.

Examples of high fantasy include J.R.R. Tolkien’s The Lord of the Rings, Brandon Sanderson’s Mistborn series, and C.S Lewis’ The Chronicles of Narnia series

Low Fantasy

Low fantasy is set in a world that is largely similar to our own, with magic or supernatural elements appearing more as intrusions or anomalies rather than as foundational aspects of the world. The primary setting is often a realistic or historical version of Earth or a world that closely resembles it.

Magic in low fantasy is typically limited and less pervasive. It often exists in the form of rare artifacts, secret knowledge, or isolated instances rather than being an integral part of everyday life. The focus is often on how these elements disrupt or influence the otherwise normal world.

The stakes in low fantasy are usually more personal and localized. Conflicts are often centered around smaller-scale issues, such as personal dilemmas, moral choices, or small-scale conspiracies.

Examples include George R.R. Martin’s A Song of Ice and Fire (though it has some high fantasy elements, its grounded, political nature leans toward low fantasy), Scott Lynch’s The Lies of Locke Lamora, Guillermo del Toro’s Pan’s Labyrinth, and Netflix’s The Witcher (though it has high fantasy elements, it includes a gritty, more realistic approach)

Urban Fantasy

Urban fantasy combines elements of fantasy with contemporary, urban settings. The magical or supernatural elements exist alongside modern technology and society, often hidden or integrated into the fabric of everyday life.

Magic and supernatural beings coexist with the modern world, often operating in secrecy or as part of hidden subcultures. The rules and systems of magic are typically designed to interact with or disrupt modern life.

Urban fantasy often focuses on personal and immediate conflicts, such as individual struggles, city-wide threats, or local mysteries. The scale is generally more intimate compared to the grand, epic scope of high fantasy.

Examples include Jim Butcher’s The Dresden Files, Patricia Briggs’ Mercy Thompson series, Joss Whedon’s Buffy the Vampire Slayer, and Neil Gaiman’s American Gods.

Setting & World-Building

High fantasy has entirely new worlds with comprehensive world building, although fantasy has realistic or historical settings with limited magical elements, and urban fantasy has contemporary settings with integrated magical or supernatural elements.

In high fantasy, magic is usually pervasive and integral to the world and its history, while in low fantasy magic is often rare and considered an anomaly or a hidden aspect, while in urban fantasy, magic exists alongside modern life, influencing or disrupting contemporary society.

Scope & Scale

High fantasy usually involves grand, epic narratives with high stakes and large-scale conflicts, while low fantasy has more personal, localized conflicts with focus on individual or small scale issues, and urban fantasy usually has intimate, often city centric conflicts involving magical elements.

Technology

High fantasy often has no magical technology or contemporary societal elements, while low fantasy closely resembles historical or realistic settings with minimal magic and in urban fantasy, modern technology and urban life interact with magic
